items.caption: academie și membru postum
items.rationale: The Academy itself lists Mihai Eminescu among posthumously elected members, with election year 1948. The qualifier is factually necessary because his life ended in 1889.

items.caption: academie și membru fondator
items.rationale: The Academy register identifies Titu Liviu Maiorescu as a founding member in 1867. The caption states the specific registered role without inferring sole founding responsibility.

items.caption: revoluționar și ținut natal
items.rationale: The Avram Iancu municipality identifies Vidra de Sus as his birthplace and describes his revolutionary organization. Vidra tourism locates this former municipality in the central Apuseni. Together these directly support a revolutionary and his native region; the statue page alone would not establish birthplace.

items.caption: oraș și regiune
items.rationale: The county council tourism account places its territory in Transylvania and discusses Cluj-Napoca as its principal city. The city development plan independently identifies Cluj-Napoca as a Transylvanian urban centre.

items.caption: oraș și salină din apropiere
items.rationale: The salt mine operator gives both entrances in Turda. County tourism places Cluj-Napoca and Turda 35 km apart on a described visitor route. Nearby is supported; the caption correctly avoids saying that the mine lies within Cluj-Napoca.

items.caption: revistă și poet publicat
items.rationale: The journal itself states in its June 1989 commemorative issue that much of Eminescu’s lifetime poetry appeared in its pages. This directly establishes a published poet, without assigning an editorial office.

items.caption: revistă și îndrumător literar
items.rationale: The journal’s historical essay describes Maiorescu withdrawing from its leadership in 1895 and his earlier circle of disciples. Literary guidance is a supported bounded description; it does not incorrectly assign the sole editor title.

items.caption: societate literară și poet
items.rationale: The national literature museum explicitly names Eminescu among the writers who read work at Junimea meetings. Society and poet therefore describes the exact cultural association.

items.caption: societate literară și mentor
items.rationale: The museum names Maiorescu among the founders and meeting hosts. The journal explicitly calls him Junimea’s mentor. The caption accurately names this role in the literary society.

items.caption: răscoală și ținutul ei
items.rationale: The county account ties the 1784 uprising to the Romanian population of the Apuseni and its three leaders. The museum research paper explicitly describes the uprising as taking place in the Apuseni area. The caption names a setting and makes no exclusivity claim.

items.caption: chei și munții din care fac parte
items.rationale: The county tourism description explicitly places the gorge at the eastern edge of the Apuseni in the Trascău group. The geographical membership phrase is accurate in either direction.

items.caption: răscoală și regiune
items.rationale: County tourism dates the uprising led by Horea, Cloșca and Crișan to Transylvania in 1784. The region caption matches the historical setting without broadening it to all places.

items.caption: obiective din zona Turda
items.rationale: The council groups the gorge and salt mine on its southern tourism route; the mine operator fixes its location in Turda and the county gorge entry places that attraction in the surrounding area. The caption states shared vicinity, not physical containment.

notes: Reviewer did not author or install these captions.
Primary museum, journal, Academy and local-authority pages were independently retrieved.
Web open failures for several WordPress pages were resolved by direct HTTPS retrieval, not assumed to be factual failures.
Additional birthplace, distance and publication references strengthen the author’s source list.
